one_line_contribution: A pre-registered measurement of a substitution ratio S — the fraction of an ExpeL-style bank's paired accuracy gain that disappears once a GEPA-optimized instruction has been trained on the identical S_train episodes — supplemented by a token-matched compiled-bank arm (C), a whole-bank dump (M_all), a co-adaptation cell (I2), and a leakage-based positive control, on one multi-hop-QA environment plus ALFWorld.
closest_prior_work: EvoAgentBench (cited as arXiv 2607.05202) is the direct threat: it already evaluates ReasoningBank/Memento retrievers and GEPA on one shared 528/267 training/test split across four domains and three backbones, and already reports the qualitative finding this proposal predicts (GEPA nearly matching a curated reference; no automatic method positive everywhere). The proposal honorably withdraws its v2 novelty sentence, but what remains is an increment on an existing table — a combined I1xM1 cell, token matching, paired McNemar/TOST, and a ratio metric. Experience Distillation (2607.21051) is the second threat: it already computes exactly this retention-ratio shape (>=64.8% of an in-context gain surviving context distillation vs 3.8% for SFT) with weights as the rival container, so the conceptual move 'measure how much of memory's value survives relocation to another container' is not new; only the choice of container (an optimized instruction) is. I cannot independently verify any 2606-2608 identifier from my own knowledge; the pre-2026 anchors that I can check (ExpeL 2308.10144, ReasoningBank 2509.25140, Memp 2508.06433, A-MEM 2502.12110, GEPA 2507.19457) are all correct, which is a point in the proposal's favour.
strongest_objection: S is not identified as substitution. The design has no arm that raises baseline accuracy without sharing information with the bank, so the shrinkage of the memory gain from cell 2 (I0xM1 - I0xM0) to cell 6 (I1xM1 - I1xM0) is fully explained by headroom compression: I1xM0 will sit well above I0xM0, the remaining unsolved instances at I1 are the harder residue, and a bank distilled only from I0-solved episodes has less marginal purchase on them whether or not GEPA ever absorbed its content. Predictions 1, 6 and 10 are all satisfied by that pure-headroom account — moderator prediction 6 ('residual gain concentrated in the top decile of instance-to-bank similarity') is if anything what headroom compression alone would produce — and the fix/break decomposition cannot separate the two because both mechanisms reduce fixes. The positive control does not rescue this: B-dup is a paraphrased near-duplicate of the test instance, whose marginal value survives any amount of headroom compression, so it certifies the instrument only for a leakage-sized effect (likely 15-25pt), not for the 2-4pt non-substitutable residual that is actually at stake given the stated MDE of ~5.8pt. Secondary problems compound it: (a) the +/-4pt TOST margin is over half the 7.7pt denominator, so H2 can pass with an I1-side gain of 3.9pt, i.e. S ~ 0.48, and the paper would declare 'the claim (H1 and H2)' confirmed while its own directional prediction S >= 0.6 fails — the two pre-registered criteria are not aligned; (b) 'same episodes' is not same supervision, since B is distilled only from solved episodes while GEPA's reflector sees scored failures, an asymmetry that biases S upward and that B_touched (coverage) does not touch; (c) A1 was selected because it previously measured +7.7pt, so gate G1 (>=6pt) faces regression to the mean, and the failure branch 'enrich the bank once and re-measure' modifies the treatment until the denominator passes; (d) the load-bearing agent is a 120B MoE while the in-scope 27B agent is pre-registered as the null regime, so the only positive result the paper can produce lies outside the 7B-32B window the track declares in scope, and 'S is agent-relative' with n=2 agents, one of them degenerate, is a weak footing for a claim about the memory literature.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Add the accuracy-matched no-overlap control described under missing_baseline and report S both raw and headroom-corrected; without it the primary endpoint should not be called substitution. 2) Define the equivalence margin as a fraction of the measured denominator (e.g. +/-0.25 x the I0 gain) rather than a fixed +/-4pt, so H2 and the S >= 0.6 prediction cannot disagree, and power the design for that tighter margin. 3) Replace or supplement B-dup with a graded positive control whose non-substitutable value is engineered to be ~3-5pt (e.g. a small fraction of duplicate items diluted into an ordinary bank), so 'a null is a finding, not a power failure' is demonstrated at the effect size that matters rather than at a leakage-sized one. 4) Match supervision, not just episodes: build a second bank from failed as well as solved S_train episodes so the distiller and the reflector see the same outcome signal. 5) Add a third agent inside the track's 7B-32B window that shows a nonzero bank effect, so the positive result does not rest on a single out-of-scope 120B model. 6) Since this is framed as a measurement contribution, re-measure at least one published memory result (ExpeL or ReasoningBank on their own reported setting) under the protocol; as written the paper builds its own bank and audits its own delta, and so qualifies no existing claim. 7) Clarify what 'token-matched per instance' means for a frozen static block C, which by construction has one length.
missing_baseline: I1_disjoint: a GEPA instruction optimized with the identical procedure, rollout budget and seeds on a disjoint, equally sized pool of training episodes (S_train') that never fed the bank, selected or truncated so that I1_disjoint x M0 matches I1 x M0 in accuracy. The memory gain measured on top of it is the counterfactual the whole design needs: if the bank's gain collapses just as far at I1_disjoint as at I1, S is measuring headroom compression rather than information transfer, and the paper's central claim evaporates. A cheaper partial substitute would be an accuracy-matched non-optimizer instruction (best-of-N hand-written prompts, or I0 plus generic reasoning boilerplate that actually moves accuracy) — I3 does not serve this role because it is deliberately content-free and is expected to move accuracy by <20% of I1's gain. Reviewers will also ask for a bank built from failed episodes to match GEPA's supervision, and for a shuffled-instruction control at I1 to bound how much of I1's own gain is content versus formatting.
preprint_collision: The check is above average for a proposal of this kind and should be credited: it is dated (2026-09-03, prior scan 2026-08-21), reports query counts, unique-paper counts, by-id verification of 54 identifiers, names the verification channel per citation, commits the scan record, and — unusually — retracts its own v2 novelty sentence in light of EvoAgentBench and reinstates five citations it had wrongly dropped. But it is not clean. First, the collision it found is not neutralized: EvoAgentBench (2607.05202) already publishes the retriever-vs-GEPA-on-shared-trajectories table, and the residual delta the proposal claims (combined cell, token matching, paired statistics, positive control) is a methods increment on an existing result rather than a new claim, which is the main reason novelty scores where it does. Second, the verification substrate is weak by the proposal's own admission — arXiv is unreachable from the node, Semantic Scholar is rate-limited, so every post-2026-05 identifier rests on HuggingFace Papers plus web-search snippets; the v2 episode where five real papers were declared unverifiable is direct evidence that this channel produces both false negatives and, potentially, false positives, and none of these identifiers is verifiable from my own knowledge. Third, the 15 queries are counted but not listed, so a reviewer cannot tell whether the specific collision that would sink this paper was searched for at all: the proposal itself flags 'a GEPA + memory ablation in an appendix of a systems paper' as the residual risk, and that is precisely the artifact that would pre-empt cells 9 and 10 — an appendix ablation is invisible to title-level HF Papers scans, so this risk is named but not actually reduced. Fourth, the compile prediction (3) is conceded to be partially pre-empted in direction by 2608.14036, 2606.30775 and 2605.23899, which makes the secondary endpoint a quantification of a known direction rather than a test. Net: a thorough, honest check that establishes there is no exact duplicate, but that also documents why the remaining novelty is thin.
